name: Segáis

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Vol. Iii. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, pp. 27–39.

text: Segáis (Segais) is an Irish mythological site and goddess. In the tale of Bóand, goddess of the River Boyne, Segáis is the name of a secret well of wisdom. Some call it Connla's Well. Others place it high in the mountains of Slieve Bloom. Still others read it as the source of the Boyne itself. The well gave wisdom to any who drank from it or ate the fish of its waters. Bóand chose to visit the well despite the ban. The water rose in three waves, struck her, and carried her to the sea. Koch records that only Nechtan and his three servants could approach. The same fate struck Sínann, the goddess of the River Shannon. The well is the root of two great Irish rivers. In the Dindshenchas the Boyne is called the river of Segáis.
